title: Amount of New Area Painted Each Day
statement:
A long wall is a number line split into unit cells, where cell `x` is the stretch from `x` to `x + 1`. On day `i` you work on the stretch from `paint[i][0]` to `paint[i][1]`, that is, cells `paint[i][0]` up to `paint[i][1] - 1`. A cell that already has paint must never get a second coat, so each day you only paint the cells of that stretch that are still bare.

Return an array `worklog` of the same length as `paint`, where `worklog[i]` is how many new cells were painted on day `i`.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way keeps a flag per cell and walks every cell of every day, which is O(n · M) for M = 5 · 10^4 and up to 10^5 days: billions of steps. What each day needs is "how many cells in this range are still bare?" followed by "paint them all". A segment tree over the cells answers both in one descent if each node stores how many of its cells are painted. A fully painted node can be skipped outright, and a node the day's range covers completely can be filled in one step.

## Approach

1. Let `size` be the largest `end`; the tree covers cells `0` to `size - 1`, and `painted[node]` counts the painted cells in that node's range `[left, right)`.
2. `paintRange` returns 0 for a node outside `[start, end)` or one that is already full.
3. If the day covers the whole node, the new cells are `right - left - painted[node]`; mark the node full and return that.
4. Otherwise split at `mid`, paint both halves, refresh `painted[node]` from the children and return `fromLeft + fromRight`.
5. Push the result for each day into `worklog`.

## Example 1, step by step

`paint = [[1,4],[4,7],[5,8]]`, so `size = 8`. Day 0 reaches cell 1 inside `[0,2)` and the whole node `[2,4)`: 1 + 2 = 3. Day 1 covers `[4,6)` whole and cell 6: 2 + 1 = 3. Day 2 finds `[4,6)` and cell 6 already full and only cell 7 bare: 1. The answer is `[3, 3, 1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(M + n log M): the array is filled once and each day visits at most a few nodes per level.
- Space: O(M) for `painted`.

## Pitfalls

- The stretch is half-open: `[1, 4]` paints 3 cells, and `[1, 4]` and `[4, 7]` do not overlap.
- Check "already full" before descending, or repaints are counted again.
- A node marked full leaves its children stale; that is safe only because full nodes are never entered again.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `size` | number of cells the tree covers |
| `painted` | painted-cell count for each tree node |
| `node`, `left`, `right` | a tree node and its cell range `[left, right)` |
| `start`, `end` | the day's range |
| `added`, `fromLeft`, `fromRight` | new cells painted in a node or its halves |
| `worklog` | the answer, one count per day |

narration.2: The tree only needs to reach the furthest end of any day.
narration.4: Grow size to cover this day's end.
narration.6: painted[node] will count how many cells in that node's range already have paint.
narration.8: Paint [start, end) inside this node's range [left, right) and return how many cells were new.
narration.9: The node lies entirely outside the day's range...
narration.12: Every cell in this node is already painted...
narration.13: ...so there is nothing new here and no need to look deeper.
narration.15: The day's range swallows this whole node.
narration.16: The bare cells in the node are exactly the new paint.
narration.17: Mark the node as fully painted; its children are never visited again.
narration.20: Partial overlap: split the node's range in half.
narration.21: Paint the overlapping part of the left half.
narration.22: Paint the overlapping part of the right half.
narration.23: Refresh this node's count from its two children.
narration.24: Report the new cells found in both halves.
narration.29: Paint the day's range starting at the root, which covers [0, size).
narration.31: worklog holds the new area painted on each day.
